**The Last Letter**

I found it tucked between the pages of an old, yellowed novel—*The Shadow of the Wind* by Carlos Ruiz Zafón, though I don’t own that book. The letter was crumpled, the ink faded but still legible. It read:

*"Dear [Name],*

*I don’t know how to say this without breaking something inside me. The thing I told you was a lie. Not the big one—you already knew that. But the small ones. The ones that added up. The way I’d say I was fine when I wasn’t. The way I’d smile when I was hurting. The way I’d pretend I didn’t care when I did.*

*I’m sorry. I wish I could take it back. But I can’t. So I’m writing this instead. Maybe it’ll mean something to you. Maybe it won’t. Either way, I hope you know how much I loved you. Even when I didn’t say it.*

*Forever yours,*
*[Name]"*

I held it in my hands, the paper brittle with age. The name at the bottom was crossed out, as if the writer had changed their mind. The date was 1998. I was 12.

I didn’t know who had written it. I didn’t know who it was for. But I knew it was real. The kind of real that lingers, even when the rest of the world forgets.

I kept it in my pocket for the rest of the night, turning it over in my fingers like a secret. The next morning, I burned it in the fireplace. The ashes scattered into the air, but the words stayed with me.

Sometimes, I wonder if someone else has ever held a letter like that. A letter that wasn’t meant to be read. A letter that was meant to be burned. A letter that was meant to be forgotten.

But not all secrets are meant to stay buried. Some are meant to be let go of. Some are meant to be written down. Some are meant to be burned.

And some are meant to be kept.

I don’t know which one this was. But I know I’ll never forget it.
